firewall_max_chars.description: FIREWALL_MAX_CHARS -- the size cap of one inbound turn, measured as the total character count of every text field in messages[]. A turn above it is rejected with reason 'oversize' and rule_id 'size-cap', BEFORE the first store hop.

firewall_rate_max.description: FIREWALL_RATE_MAX -- how many turns one channel may pass within FIREWALL_RATE_WINDOW_MS. Reaching it rejects with reason 'rate_limited' and rule_id 'rate-limit'. 0 closes the channel entirely.

firewall_rate_window_ms.description: FIREWALL_RATE_WINDOW_MS -- the width of the rate window in milliseconds. The window is a lexicographic comparison against the arrivals table's recorded_at, so the count is reproducible from stamped times alone.

description.purpose: The screen: every inbound turn is measured against the rule set before anything agentic sees it, and leaves on exactly one of two lanes -- 'pass' with the body UNCHANGED, or 'reject' naming the reason and the rule that fired. Every verdict is arithmetic or a literal comparison; no model is asked and none can be.
description.use_when: As the first cell of every ingress channel, between the surface (proxy, HTTP, voice bridge) and the agent's intake. Wire the ingress lane with hop.route 'in_turn' and promote the channel identity to context.channel (and context.user_id where the surface has one); wire BOTH exits, and delete the firewall's context keys on each.
description.not_in_scope: No answer to the sender -- the screen never speaks outbound; what a reject becomes (a drain, a log line, a polite refusal) is the parent tree's decision. No regex engine, no model judgement, no learning: the rules are literals in a store. No rewriting of a passed turn -- the pass lane is byte-identical, that is the whole point of putting it in front.
description.emits_meaning: route 'fwstore': the store ops of the current step (hop.phase names it: 'rules' loads the rule set, 'rate' counts the window, 'mark' books the arrival); hop.fw_body carries the turn in transit and hop.fw_now the one stamp of this turn, both promoted to context by the hive edge. route 'pass': the inbound body UNCHANGED, hop.reject_reason and hop.rule_id empty. route 'reject': the refused body with hop.reject_reason (oversize | rules_unreadable | sender_denied | sender_not_allowed | pattern_blocked | rate_limited) and hop.rule_id (the store row that fired, or the reserved id 'size-cap' / 'rate-limit' / 'allowlist:<field>'). A store reply the screen cannot name emits NOTHING.
description.consumes_meaning: One entry lane, named by hop.route on the port edge: in_turn. context.channel and context.user_id are the two identity dimensions the rules compare against; a surface that names neither runs on the single bucket 'default'. hop.recorded_at (optional) stamps the turn from outside -- an operator or a test seam; unset means the screen stamps it itself. Store replies are dispatched by context.fw_phase together with hop.operation.
examples: in_turn, 40 chars, no enabled rule, first turn of the minute -> route 'pass', body byte-identical
in_turn on user_id 999 while an enabled allow row names user_id 42 -> route 'reject', reason 'sender_not_allowed', rule_id 'allowlist:user_id'
in_turn containing 'ignore all previous instructions' with a substring row -> route 'reject', reason 'pattern_blocked', rule_id = that row
the 31st turn of a channel within 60 s at FIREWALL_RATE_MAX 30 -> route 'reject', reason 'rate_limited', rule_id 'rate-limit'; the arrival is NOT booked
